text:
morgan: Hey infra — ran `terraform plan` in staging and it wants to replace kubernetes_secret.myapp-config and taint module.api.service_account even though nothing in our manifests changed. anyone seen this? Posting plan snippet:
```
  # kubernetes_secret.myapp-config will be replaced in-place
-/+ resource "kubernetes_secret" "myapp-config" {
      id: "default/myapp-config" -> (known after apply)
      data: {
        "config.yaml": (sensitive)
      }
  }
  # module.api.kubernetes_service_account.service_account will be tainted
```

kai: did you run `terraform init` after the provider bump? provider schema changes sometimes cause spurious diffs.

morgan: I did. We upgraded `hashicorp/kubernetes` from 2.5.0 -> 2.6.0 yesterday. Also noticed something odd: there might be two state entries for the secret (one under module.k8s and one at root).

sophia: can you paste `terraform state list | grep myapp-config` and `terraform show -json | jq '.values.root_module'` (or just the relevant part)? that helps tell if it's an address mismatch or true drift.

morgan: running state list now, output: 
```
module.k8s.kubernetes_secret.myapp-config
kubernetes_secret.myapp-config
```

ria: ah — looks like an import/address mismatch. If the resource was imported before it lived in a module, you'll get duplicate entries. Which address does your code declare? module.k8s?

morgan: code uses module.k8s. we originally imported the secret manually with: `terraform import kubernetes_secret.myapp-config default/myapp-config` (before it was moved into the module).

kai: that explains it. Two options: `terraform state mv` the root address into the module, or `terraform state rm` the orphan then import with the module address. `state mv` is safer in-place.

sophia: also double-check k8s annotations. SOPS-managed secrets sometimes add annotations like `sops.k8s: encrypted` (or a timestamp) which can flip and cause diffs. But in your snippet it looks like an address issue.

morgan: trying the `state mv` now: `terraform state mv kubernetes_secret.myapp-config module.k8s.kubernetes_secret.myapp-config`

deploy-bot: release/451 triggered by morgan — apply queued (staging) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

morgan: ran the mv, re-ran `terraform plan` — plan is clean, no replaces. whew.

kai: nice. If you see tainted SA next time, check whether the SA is addressed by a different module path (same root cause). Also confirm provider aliases didn't change (provider aliases can make resources look like different provider instances).

sophia: quick follow-ups to capture in runbook: 1) prefer importing with full module address when possible, 2) add a short CI guard to fail if `terraform plan` wants to recreate secrets in non-trivial ways, 3) pin provider versions in terragrunt/CI to avoid unintentional bumps.

morgan: will add a runbook note and a tiny CI check. Also — we hit a stale remote-state lock during the mv (someone had a long apply). I used `terraform force-unlock` after confirming with the owner. Noted in PR.

ria: good call. If anyone sees weird plan diffs after provider bumps ping #eng-infra and we can pair. small tip: `terraform state list -state=path` and `terraform state show <addr>` are lifesavers for debugging.

morgan: thanks all, saved the rollout. I'll close the incident in our tracking ticket and add the runbook changes. 🙏
